attributes.probed_form: MECHANICAL RECIPE, three steps, scripted in lane scratch (not promoted). (1) Segment the file at depth-0 brace boundaries into function definitions and inter-function GAPS. (2) Emit verbatim the PROLOGUE -- everything through the .bss definitions and enemy_bss_order -- then HOIST every gap's declaration lines (extern / forward declaration / typedef / #define) into one block in their ORIGINAL RELATIVE ORDER, keeping with each function only its trailing documenting-comment run and its #pragma bracket. Relative order is what makes the hoist inert: the compiler sees the identical declaration SEQUENCE it saw before, and a declaration emits no storage. (3) Emit the functions in the target order, with a whole-TU forward-declaration block (66 prototypes, generated from the definition heads) placed at the END of the hoisted declarations -- after every typedef and struct tag they reference -- so a callee defined after its caller still compiles.
attributes.residual:
THREE FUNCTIONS REGRESSED ACROSS THE PASS AND ALL THREE HAD ONE CAUSE: a `#pragma opt_propagation off` region whose extent is DEFINITION ORDER, so reordering definitions relocates which functions it covers. Recorded as claim.law.EO_a-bare-pragma-reset-does-not-close-opt_propagation-off-and-a-text-reorder-relocates-the-leak-across-the-tu.20260904.v1. Two variants appeared, and the second is a hazard of the REWRITE TOOL rather than of the source:
  (a) SOURCE VARIANT. do_enemies' body opens `#pragma opt_propagation off` and closes it with a bare `#pragma reset`, which does not close it. Pre-reorder do_enemies sat at source line 6786 of 7521 and the leak covered 4 functions; post-reorder it is at target position 42 of 62 and covers 19. damage_enemy (real 66 -> 282, frame 176 -> 160) and fn_8004DF58 (EXACT -> STRUCTURAL, 315 against the target's 316, losing the target's `addi r29,r3,0` at +0x14c) both returned to their pre-reorder scores under one added `#pragma opt_propagation reset` after do_enemies' closing brace, with no source change to either. init_enemy then regressed (frame 80 -> 88, opcode multiset IDENTICAL 136/136, 10 aligned IMMEDIATE frame rows) because it had been living inside the leak, and was closed by bracketing it explicitly.
  (b) TOOL VARIANT, and the one worth warning the next rewriter about. The segmenter consumed any `#pragma` line following a top-level item as that item's trailing CLOSER. That is right after a function body, where `#pragma opt_propagation reset` is glued to the closing brace with no blank line, and WRONG after a typedef: `typedef struct EnemyMovePage05 {...};` is followed by move_logic05's OPENER `#pragma opt_propagation off`, which the tool therefore carried into the hoisted declaration block -- above every function in the file. The whole first 40% of the TU then compiled with propagation off, and the visible symptom was closest_enemy's webfrank pin aborting with `closest_enemy: input hash 1f0dc55... != expected df7ab68...`, diagnosed by t16_rederive_body as `REFUSED by the rule's own guards: non-register instruction bits differ at +0x8: 0x00000008` -- i.e. the frame, `stwu r1,-192` against `stwu r1,-184`, read from `fnasm --raw`. Restrict closer-consumption to FUNCTION items and to the literal closer strings (`opt_propagation reset`, `opt_common_subs reset`, `dont_inline off`); openers live in the NEXT function's leading gap and must stay there. A pragma-count and open/close-pairing check over the rewritten file (28 lines here, balanced) catches this in zero builds.

WHAT DID *NOT* GO WRONG, measured, because the obvious fear is the wrong one. The declaration HOIST is inert. Hoisting can only change codegen where a call site previously had NO declaration in scope, and the whole implicit set in this TU was three names: DoEnemyAction and StartItemGrid are declared nowhere in the file (so hoisting cannot reach them), and NextGridItem was declared at line 7227 below closest_enemy's unprototyped call at line 339. That last one was initially SUSPECTED of costing closest_enemy its frame and was excluded from the hoist as a precaution; the exclusion was tested directly at 11e1ff440 by hoisting it back, and closest_enemy's raw prologue reads `stwu r1,-192(r1) / stmw r23,84(r1)` with the pin replaying green -- so the suspicion was WRONG and the declaration now sits with the others (commit 358ef2e5b). Separately, the whole-TU prototype block was A/B'd ALONE against the unmodified file (original definition order, prototypes inserted before closest_enemy) and measured GATE OK with zero rows, which is what proves the 66 prototypes are not themselves a codegen change. The one genuine declaration-placement case is a CONFLICTING duplicate rather than an implicit call: `extern void SetEnemyObj();` (K&R) at line 5185 and `extern void SetEnemyObj(Enemy*, s32, s32)` at line 7426, where damage_enemy's `SetEnemyObj((u8*)e, ...)` compiles only while the prototyped form is BELOW it -- the compiler said so directly (`cannot convert 'unsigned char *' to 'struct Enemy *'`). Leaving the full prototype at its original first-legal position in the new order (immediately before init_enemy) keeps the reorder at ZERO source changes outside definition order.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Run the pairing check over the 22 other NonMatching units textorder currently flags as MISORDERED: if none of them carries a dangling pragma opener, the hazard is unique to enemy.c and does not deserve tool surface.
hypothesis.count_consequence: count-neutral by construction: it is a source screen, not a codegen change.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- measured on this TU at 2185b3155: `grep -c '#pragma' src/game/enemy/enemy.c` is 28 and every opener now pairs, but before the fix do_enemies' opener paired only with a bare `#pragma reset` and the three functions downstream of it regressed exactly as the check would have predicted. The check is source-only and costs no build.
hypothesis.statement: textorder.py should ship a PRAGMA-PAIRING screen alongside its order verdict: for the unit it is about to declare MISORDERED, pair every `#pragma <name> off|on` with a matching `#pragma <name> reset` and report any opener left dangling. A dangling opener means some suffix of the TU compiles under a non-default option set, the reorder will change which functions that suffix contains, and the lane needs to bracket those functions explicitly BEFORE moving anything. All three of this pass's regressions were that one condition, and no other check in the project looks for it.
